title: Falsy error context values are silently dropped from metadata
reasoning: Several exception constructors mirror caller-supplied context into attributes, but metadata inclusion is gated with bool(field_value) or any(fields.values()). Valid falsy values such as status_code=0, retry_after=0, actual_size=0, max_size=0, or timeout_seconds=0 are retained on the exception attributes while disappearing from metadata. That creates inconsistent machine-readable error payloads for callers that serialize BaseAppError.metadata rather than inspecting type-specific attributes.
reproduction: Instantiate ParseTimeoutError('timeout', timeout_seconds=0) or InputSizeLimitError('limit', actual_size=0, max_size=0) and inspect error.metadata; the provided size/timeout fields are absent while the attributes are set.
recommendation: Treat None as the absent value for optional scalar metadata instead of using truthiness. For trust-boundary metadata, include metadata when boundary_name is not None or any provided field value is not None, and consider filtering only absent fields if null metadata is not desired.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were included for this feature, and the excerpt contains no assertions covering metadata parity for falsy but valid context values.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add focused tests that construct LLMAPIError(status_code=0), LLMRateLimitError(retry_after=0), InputSizeLimitError(actual_size=0, max_size=0), and ParseTimeoutError(timeout_seconds=0), then assert those values are present in metadata and still mirrored to attributes.
minimumFixScope: Update the metadata helper predicates in base.py and any affected trust-boundary helper logic, then add regression tests for falsy context values.
